title.value: Robust Contrastive Learning against Noisy Views
title.justification: The title clearly indicates the focus of the paper is on improving the robustness of contrastive learning methods, specifically addressing the challenge of noisy data views.

extractions.description: The paper introduces a new contrastive loss function, RINCE, which enhances contrastive learning by being robust against noisy views in data. The method is theoretically justified through its links to robust symmetric losses for noisy classification and is proven to improve performance across various modalities like image, video, and graph data. The RINCE loss is modality-agnostic and can easily replace InfoNCE in current frameworks.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper's primary focus is on improving contrastive learning techniques and enhancing data robustness. It does not directly address any climate or ecological sustainable development issues.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: In this work, we propose a new contrastive loss function that is robust against noisy views.

primary_category.justification: There is no direct relevance of this paper to climate or ecological sustainable development as it focuses on technical enhancements in machine learning algorithms.
primary_category.quote: The literature suggests that contrastive learning produces suboptimal representations in the presence of noisy views, e.g., false positive pairs with no apparent shared information.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper does not address any secondary themes related to climate or ecological sustainable development.
secondary_categories.quote: We provide rigorous theoretical justifications by showing connections to robust symmetric losses for noisy binary classification.

primary_sub_category.justification: No specific sub-category aligns with the central themes of this paper as it’s focused on technical improvements in deep learning methodologies unrelated to sustainability.
primary_sub_category.quote: We demonstrate our approach on real-world scenarios of image, video, and graph contrastive learning.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: Since the paper does not engage with climate or ecological sustainability themes, no secondary sub-categories are applicable.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Contrastive learning relies on an assumption that positive pairs contain related views, e.g., patches of an image or co-occurring multimodal signals of a video.

applications.justification: The primary application discussed in the paper is enhancing the robustness of contrastive learning algorithms against noisy data.
applications.quote: We propose RINCE, a new contrastive learning objective that is robust against noisy views of data.

new_primary_category.justification: The scopes defined do not cover the technical nature of this paper itself; thus, no new primary category is required.
new_primary_category.quote: For images, the views are typically constructed by applying common data augmentation techniques.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: As the paper is purely technical, no new sub-category fitting within climate or ecological sustainable development is necessary.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: We relate noisy views to noisy labels by interpreting contrastive learning as binary classification.
